title: Squared derivatives under last-coordinate restriction
statement:
Let $n\ge 0$, let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$, let $b\in\{0,1\}$, and let $x\in\{0,1\}^n$. The sum of the squares of all coordinate half-differences of $f$ at $(x,b)$ equals the sum of the squares of the coordinate half-differences of the restriction $f_b(z)=f(z,b)$ at $x$, plus the square of the last-coordinate half-difference of $f$ at $x$:
\[\sum_{i=0}^{n}(D_i f(x,b))^2=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(D_i f_b(x))^2+\left(\frac{f(x,0)-f(x,1)}{2}\right)^2.\]
replaced: Let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$, $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$, and $d=(f_0-f_1)/2$. Then $\sum_{i<n+1}(D_i f(x,b))^2=\sum_{i<n}(D_i f_b(x))^2+d(x)^2$ for every $x,b$, with $D_i$ the coordinate half-difference.
